title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: A New York jury found the Chinese firm lied about its Iran business.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November 25, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: US jury convicts Huawei of Iran sanctions violations and stealing trade secrets
stories.why_important: A New York jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 charges. The charges include lying to banks about its Iran business and plotting to steal US trade secrets. The verdict increases Washington's pressure on China's biggest telecom equipment maker and raises its cost of doing business.
stories.what_overlooked: Huawei says it will appeal, so penalties are not final. The charges also cover North Korea and raise sanctions risk for banks that handled Huawei's payments.
stories.prediction: Prosecutors may seek a court monitor or new penalties within days. A monitor would put US oversight inside Huawei.

stories.story_title: Solomon Islands names Australia its main security partner in treaty that excludes China
stories.why_important: The treaty makes Australia the islands' main security partner and bars foreign military bases, shutting China out. Honiara also told Beijing it will end their 2022 security pact, a reported move that would mark a clear Pacific realignment.
stories.what_overlooked: The treaty is also a bet on Australian money, not just security. Local economic power will decide whether Honiara stays aligned.
stories.prediction: China's foreign ministry may respond within days with aid or trade warnings. A sharp reply would show Beijing sees the treaty as a real loss.

stories.story_title: Putin says Ukraine keeps hitting Russian refineries and promises retaliation
stories.why_important: Putin said Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries despite Trump's request to stop, and he promised to hit back. Several Russian regions have limited retail fuel sales, showing the drone campaign is hurting Russia inside the country.
stories.what_overlooked: Kyiv says it will stop hitting energy targets only when Moscow does. Ukraine's foreign minister told Putin to end the war instead of complaining.
stories.prediction: Russia may strike Ukrainian power plants within days. New nationwide blackouts would show Putin has begun the retaliation he promised.

quick_hits.text: Israeli strikes killed seven people in Gaza, including a senior Hamas internal security official, Palestinian officials said, despite a ceasefire in place since last year.
Spain holds a general election on Sunday, with polls showing Alberto Núñez Feijóo within reach of unseating Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongly deported to El Salvador, left the US for Spain under a deal, ending a legal fight that reached the Supreme Court.
A car bomb outside regional government offices in Villavicencio, Colombia, injured 23 people as rebel and drug-gang violence spreads into cities.
The UN Security Council debated how AI and drones are reshaping war, as Pakistan urged human control over nuclear launch decisions.
China's Shenzhou-24 carried Pakistan's first astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong station, the first foreigner to visit it.

views.framing: The verdict is a legitimate US legal finding of Huawei's guilt, tied to Washington's national-security concerns.
views.quote: The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.

views.framing: The case is a long US criminal proceeding that convicted Huawei on most counts while acquitting it of racketeering.
views.quote: But the jury found the technology company not guilty of conspiracy to obstruct justice or conspiracy under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organisations Act, or Ric

views.framing: Beijing and Huawei reject the US verdict as political suppression, framing the case as US pressure on Chinese firms.
views.quote: Beijing criticised the US after a jury found Huawei guilty of 10 criminal counts, including trade secrets theft and bank fraud.

perspective_grid.blindspot: The US is preparing to raise tariffs on China, the EU and other economies after reviewing policies that favor surplus production. The move could disrupt global supply chains and raise costs for businesses and consumers.

developing.text: About 130 countries refused the COP31 president's final text over weak fossil-fuel language, sinking the talks; the next summit will be in Ethiopia.
Reporting traced a network shipping Nvidia AI chips to China despite US export rules, as Jensen Huang returned as CEO this week.
